items.content:
Back in March, my engagement dropped by 20%.

Less likes, lower impressions and my follower growth slowed down.

I did one thing to fix it…

Focused on commenting because it was something I'd been neglecting.

Great content isn't enough anymore.

You have to be connecting with others, adding new connections and commenting daily. 

But you need a system.

1. Find the right posts to comment on

→ Big creators in your niche for visibility
→ Mid-sized creators at your level for relationships
→ Your ideal clients for visibility 

2. What a great comment looks like

→ Give your actual opinion
→ Agree or disagree respectfully
→ Hype someone (my personal fave)
→ Add a perspective the post didn't cover
→ Share a short story that backs up the point

3. What a bad comment looks like

→ "Great post. So true."
→ A summary of what they just said
→ Anything that could apply to any post ever written

4. Build your comment ladder

→ 5 comments on big creators daily
→ 3 comments on mid creators daily
→ 2 comments on peers daily

5. How often to comment

→ 30 mins before you post to warm the feed
→ 15 mins after you post to build momentum
→ Daily whether you post that day or not

6. What to track

→ Impressions on comments
→ Profile views after commenting
→ DMs that start from a comment

Your comments are content too.

They're where you can have fun, show personality, be silly.

All those things build your brand.

Don't neglect them.

♻️ Repost to help your network 


How many comments do you leave per day?

items.content:
DEMAND PLANNING (NEXT LEVEL)
Most people forecast. Few actually plan.
Everyone knows the basics: What • When • How Much
But real demand planning starts when you ask:
Why is demand changing—and what will it cost if I’m wrong?

1. Not all demand behaves the same 
Stable → optimize cost
Seasonal → manage timing
Trend → control scaling risk
Irregular → protect with buffers
Misclassification = wrong inventory, wrong decisions.

2. There is no universal forecasting model
Stop applying one method to all SKUs. Match model to behavior. Segment demand properly. Accept trade-offs (accuracy vs responsiveness)

3. Accuracy is incomplete without direction
MAPE tells you how wrong, Bias tells you where you’re leaning
High bias = overstock or stockouts
Low visibility = unstable decision

4. Forecast = business impact
Every number affects: Inventory investment, Service level, Lost sales or excess stock, this is not reporting, this is financial decision-making.

5. Discipline is what creates results
Before ordering: Validate trend vs noise. Check real demand drivers.
When issues happen:
Overstock → check bias
Stockout → check missed signals
And always: No adjustment without a reason. No decision without impact.
Bottom line, High accuracy alone is not success.
The real goal is balance: Service level • Inventory • Cost

That’s what separates a planner from a decision-maker.

items.content:
The Algorithm Insights Report 2026 is built on 1.3M+ posts and 80,000+ profiles.
 It tells you what mistakes to avoid. Where each format breaks. How to get the most out of it. But it doesn't tell you which formats to use.
 
That part is yours. Every creator builds their own mix based on strengths, goals, and what they actually enjoy making.
 
And before anyone says "the algorithm doesn't matter" I double dare you to publish a 50-slide carousel. A 12-minute video. A short post with an external link aimed at conversion. Then come back and tell me the algorithm doesn't matter.
 
It does. 
The report shows you the guardrails. 
But it's only you decide what to drive inside them.
 
Here's how I use (or ignore) the 8 formats right now:
 
𝗗𝗼𝗰𝘂𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 → 𝗺𝘆 𝗳𝗮𝘃𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗲, 𝗻𝗼 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁. Educational content, process breakdowns, authority pieces. Under 10 slides, short copy. The report says 9.2 is the sweet spot. I'm aligned here.
 
𝗧𝗲𝘅𝘁 + 𝗶𝗺𝗮𝗴𝗲 → 𝗺𝗼𝘀𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗶𝗻𝗳𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗽𝗵𝗶𝗰𝘀. Dense information in one visual, or a glimpse into events and meetings. Copy carries as much weight as the image.
 
𝗧𝗲𝘅𝘁 𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 → 𝗜 𝗯𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗹𝘆 𝘂𝘀𝗲 𝗶𝘁. The algorithm has warmed up to it again. I still feel naked without a visual. When it's just words, your writing has to do everything. I'd rather play to my strengths.
 
𝗡𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗼 → 𝗼𝗻 𝗺𝘆 𝘁𝗼-𝗱𝗼 𝗹𝗶𝘀𝘁. Couch Talk with Richard had a strong run in 2023–2024. Then I almost forgot about video. It's a heavy production process and I still prefer writing. Honest question: should I start a YouTube channel instead?
 
𝗣𝗼𝗹𝗹𝘀 → 𝗮 𝗹𝗼𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝗵𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗺. 𝗜 𝗱𝗼𝗻'𝘁. Used well, they're brilliant. I run them when I'm genuinely curious how others handle what's happening on LinkedIn. Some answers are surprisingly funny.
 
𝗔𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗹𝗲𝘀 & 𝗻𝗲𝘄𝘀𝗹𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀 → 𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗺𝘆 𝗳𝗮𝘃𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗲. My Sunday newsletter has the highest conversion rate of anything I publish. Depth, thought leadership, real connection. And increasingly important for SEO and GEO.
 
𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗸𝗲𝗱𝗜𝗻 𝗟𝗶𝘃𝗲 → 𝗴𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀. 𝗛𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿. The infrastructure still intimidates me. But if video is on my list, Live probably should be too.
 
The report gives you the rules. 
Your mix is yours to build.
 
→ Full breakdown of all 8 formats (with the data) is in Chapter 3 of the Algorithm Insights Report 2026. 

Get your copy here: https://lnkd.in/eZMq8w_F
 
One question I'd love your take on: 
→ Should I start my own YouTube channel? Yes or no?

How to climb all 4 layers of Claude in one weekend:

(even if you just signed up yesterday)

✦ Level 1: Claude Chat (Saturday morning)

Go to claude .com/download. Install the app.
Pay the $20. Select Opus 4.6 + Extended Thinking. 
Connect Slack, Drive, Notion through Connectors.
Stop writing long prompts. Prompt this instead:
"I want to [TASK] for [SUCCESS CRITERIA]. Use AskUserQuestion before you start."

Most people stay here forever.
You're leaving 90% of Claude untouched.
Claude Basics: how-to-claude.ai.

——

✦ Level 2: Claude Cowork (Saturday afternoon)

Go to 'Cowork'. Create a folder "Claude-Cowork."
4 subfolders. About me, template, project & outputs
Create about-me .md: what you do, how you do.
Create anti-ai-style .md: words you'd never say. 
Set Global Instructions (Settings → Cowork → Edit): 
"Always read my files first, never edit my originals, deliver everything to CLAUDE OUTPUTS."

You just killed prompting.
From now on, your prompt is 2 lines + your folder.
Move on to Cowork: claude-co.work

——

✦ Level 3: Skills + Plugins (Sunday morning)

Open Cowork. Type: "Use the skill-creator to help me build a skill for [your most repeated task]."
Claude interviews you. Answer and be specific.
It generates a SKILL .md. Test it: "When would you use this skill?" If the description is vague, fix it.
Upload: Settings → Capabilities → Skills → Upload. 
Now it fires automatically. No slash command.
Install Plugins: Cowork > Customize > Browse plugin

Skills with about-me .md. Skill handles the process. 
Voice file handles tone. Two layers simultaneously.
Set up Claude Skills: https://lnkd.in/g9MQUC-Z

——

✦ Level 4: Code + Computer (Sunday afternoon)

Click the Code tab. Create a folder. Connect GitHub 
(free account → Settings → Connectors).
Prompt: "Create a GitHub repo named [project]. Code everything. Don't ask for permissions."
Download VS Code. Install the Claude extension. 
Turn on "Skip Permissions" to go 100x faster.
After your session, paste this: "Create a CLAUDE .md file with everything you learned about this project." Now Claude remembers your fonts, colors, and structure forever.
Claude code guide: https://lnkd.in/gsRhsFxT

Claude Computer: Settings → Desktop app → turn on Browser use + Computer use. 
Connect your phone with Dispatch. Text a task. 
Schedule a recurring task: left sidebar → Scheduled → write the prompt → pick the frequency.
Claude Computer: https://lnkd.in/dSaSqRxw

This is where you stop working inside Claude.
Claude starts working on your computer.

——

Saturday, you were prompting like it's ChatGPT.
Sunday, Claude is running your screen, building your website, & sending you text updates.

That's all 4 layers. In one weekend.

items.content:
If I had to start my LinkedIn again, this would be my exact plan: 

(To hit 10,000 followers in 90 days)

→ 0 to 500: Prove you exist
↳ Pick one outcome (growth, clients, authority)
↳ Choose 2-4 content pillars & stick to them
↳ Comment on 10 posts every day
↳ Post 3 x per week minimum
↳ Write as you talk

☑️ Your only goal here is not quitting.

→ 500 to 2K: Get specific.
↳ Name your audience (title, industry, problems)
↳ Study top performing posts & do more of that
↳ Reply to every comment for 60 mins after posting
↳ Share what's working and what failed

☑️ People trust progress, not perfection.

→ 2K to 5K: Build the engine
↳ One story-driven post per week
↳ Save every high-performing post
↳ Comment like it's content
↳ Track saves and DMs

☑️ If your DMs are quiet, your content isn't converting.

→ 5K to 10K: Repurpose and convert
↳ Turn your top 5 posts into carousels & infographics
↳ One conversion post per week (results & proof)
↳ Collaborate with creators at your level
↳ Earn trust through your content

☑️ At this stage, consistency is the product.

If you want to grow your LinkedIn…

You have to be strategic. 
You have to be consistent. 
You have to be intentional. 

Do those things and you will grow. 

♻️ Repost so your network sees this.


P.S. Which stage are you at?
